drhp.business: Linde India operates through two segments: Gases & Related Products, which supplies oxygen, nitrogen, argon and specialty gases via onsite pipeline systems, bulk liquid distribution networks and packaged gas solutions (including a healthcare portfolio of medical gases for hospitals), and Project Engineering, which designs and delivers air separation plants and engineering solutions supporting industrial development. As part of the global Linde plc network, the company combines international capabilities with local market insight.

risks.note: Increasing trade protectionism, geopolitical tensions and uncertainties in international markets pose risks to supply chains, energy markets and capital flows; a slowdown in global economic growth could affect demand from key industrial sectors, and currency fluctuations may impact input costs.
Inflationary pressures in key commodities and rising energy costs are a concern given the energy-intensive nature of industrial gas production.
risks.risk: Domestic inflation and energy cost risk

risks.note: Performance is closely linked to core sectors such as steel, refining, chemicals, healthcare and infrastructure; a slowdown in these sectors could reduce demand. The business model, including long-term onsite supply arrangements, exposes the Company to customer concentration and sectoral cyclicality.
Capacity additions by industry participants may exert pressure on pricing and margins.
Supply chain disruptions, availability of critical equipment, and reliability of large production facilities such as Air Separation Units may affect plant uptime and service delivery.
risks.risk: Operational risk at production and supply chain facilities

risks.note: Increasing digitalization of operations exposes the Company to cyber-attacks on plants and business systems, which could impact business continuity if not adequately managed.

Exposure to environmental and climate-related risks, including those arising from the transition towards a low-carbon economy and increasing regulatory focus on sustainability; regulatory or policy changes may also influence infrastructure spending, an important demand driver.

The Company was in receipt of an Order (ref. WTM/AB/CFID/CFID-SEC3/30578/2024-25 dated 24 July 2024) passed by SEBI under Sections 11(1), 11(4) and 11B of the SEBI Act, 1992; the Directors' Report states there were no significant/material orders impacting going-concern status, but the order itself is disclosed.
